items.title: Hafta letters: Political unrest, AI anxiety and an app that needs an update
items.summary: Eldrich I’ve been a listener since 2013, and a subscriber since 2015. I’m writing to offer a critique of Anand V’s general comments and hypothesise about why some subscribers take issue. In Hafta 612, Manisha asked Anand about orchestration being behind the recent global protests, and a second question about the plight of Gen Z. Anand’s response was typical of an Indian bureaucrat - meandering and lacking substance. He invoked Napoleon, civic order, India-Pakistan parallels, but did not answer any questions. Anand, respectfully, not every opinion needs a hedge. You refuse to generalise Gen Z folks – fine – but you can still make meaningful, broad observations. You can safely generalise that Gen Z is in a tough economic spot - that’s generally true. This is typical of most of Anand’s commentary: five minutes in, the question is lost, and we are suddenly discussing Vajpayee or Napoleon. *** Manjil Dear Hafta Team, It's great to see an ‘AI’ interview in NL. Mathematicians like me are going through an existential crisis; it might make a good story (I am sure several of us are among your subscribers). In any case, I hope you'll do a panel discussion on AI and how it will change society

items.title: India needs dedicated IP courts: Delhi High Court Justice Prathiba M Singh
items.summary: Delhi High Court Justice Prathiba M Singh has called for the establishment of dedicated intellectual property (IP) courts across India. Speaking at a discussion on Shaping the Legal Architecture of Viksit Bharat 2047 , Justice Singh suggested amending the Commercial Courts Act to establish specialised IP courts at the district and High Court levels. " I have no doubt in my mind that we need to create uniform IP courts across the country ," she said. She explained that specialised courts would facilitate judicial training and the development of consistent jurisprudence. The discussion was organised by the University of Chicago Center in Delhi, Nani Palkhivala Foundation and General Counsels' Association of India (GCAI). It was moderated by Sanjeev Gemawat . Viksit Bharat Panel Justice Singh also proposed the creation of a national JUDICIAL STACK, on the lines of INDIA STACK which could improve judicial efficiency and ease of judicial administration. " If we create the Judicial Stack and give API access, newer solutions could be found considering the pendency of 5 crore cases in our courts ," she said. items.title: Sikkim High Court suspends district judge who told Supreme Court he was targeted for complaining against HC judge
items.summary: The Sikkim High Court has suspended District and Sessions Judge at Mangan, Prajwal Khatiwada, weeks after he approached the Supreme Court alleging that he was being targeted for complaining against a then sitting High Court judge. The suspension order, dated November 4, was issued on a decision taken by the Full Court. It places him under suspension with immediate effect, pending disciplinary proceedings and until further orders. The Full Court said it was of the prima facie view that his explanations to two show-cause notices were not satisfactory and that his continuation in office was not conducive to the proper administration of justice. The order does not mention his complaint against the High Court judge or the petition he filed before Supreme Court. Grounds for suspension The first ground concerns his time as Registrar General. He is alleged to have effected promotions and upgradations without adequate legal or administrative basis and made appointments contrary to rules. The order puts the financial loss at about ₹1.64 crore. The Full Court rejected the argument that some actions had higher approval. The conference, themed Charting the Path to Effective Dispute Resolution: Strategy, Process and Outcome , will be held at The St. Regis Mumbai, Lower Parel, from 2 PM to 7.15 PM. Singapore's Senior Minister of State for Law and Transport Murali Pillai SC and Bombay High Court Justice Bharati Dangre will deliver special addresses at the conference. SIAC Chief Executive Officer Gloria Lim will deliver the opening remarks, followed by a welcome address by Davinder Singh SC , Chairman of the SIAC Board of Directors. The conference will examine how businesses and their legal teams approach commercial disputes, manage litigation risks and balance legal objectives with costs, reputation and commercial relationships. items.title: Kochi Mini Cooper crash: All four accused get bail, Suhail to be released after 10 days
items.summary: All four accused in the Mini Cooper crash that took three lives in Keralam’s Kochi were granted regular bail on Friday, November 6. The Kerala High Court ruled that prime accused Suhail Sajeev may be released after a period of 10 days. The court set no such timeline for the release of the three others, Ninav, Ameen Shah, and Joyal S Anto, LiveLaw reported . Granting bail, Justice Kauser Edapagath made note of the fact that the investigation has concluded and the accused have been held in custody for almost a month. “They have no criminal antecedents. They are students. Twice police custody has been given. Investigation, everything is over...They have been in custody for almost a month. There must be some reason for them to continue in custody," he orally observed, according to LiveLaw. The case pertains to a fatal accident at the Airport-Athani road in Kochi’s Nedumbassery on October 11. The overspeeding Mini Cooper driven by 19-year-old Suhail hit a scooter carrying three persons. All three – Gopika (22), Devika (21), and Iyas (21) – died in the accident. Suhail was found to be under the influence of alcohol.
